title: KRW formula-size conjecture with constant loss
formal:
Is there an absolute constant \(\alpha>0\) such that for every pair of positive integers \(n,m\) and every pair of nonconstant total Boolean functions \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}\), \(g:\{0,1\}^m\to\{0,1\}\),
\[L(g\circ f)\ge\alpha L(g)L(f)?\]
Here \((g\circ f)(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(m)})=g(f(x^{(1)}),\ldots,f(x^{(m)}))\) on \(m\) disjoint \(n\)-bit blocks, and \(L\) is minimum De Morgan formula leaf size. The constant is chosen before all dimensions and functions.

This card retains the constant-factor formula-size version displayed as Conjecture 5.13 in the source book. It is stronger than versions permitting a growing multiplicative loss. The original KRW paper formulates a depth-composition question; the card does not identify that question, weakened quantitative versions, and the displayed constant-loss formula statement as equivalent.
why: A formula for a composition can substitute an inner computation wherever an outer input is used, multiplying the leaf counts. A universal matching lower bound would show that alternative Boolean factorizations cannot save more than a constant factor on arbitrary block compositions. This is a strong structural statement about formulas, closely connected to the source’s superpolynomial formula lower-bound question.
status_note: The book’s displayed Conjecture 5.13 and footnote 54, the original journal paper’s Section 4, the published 2023 formula-composition bounds, and the STACS 2025 strong-composition discussion were checked on 2026-09-14. importance.reason: A structural conjecture about formula composition that could turn local lower bounds into stronger general formula lower bounds.

sentences: The selected KRW variant asks whether minimum formula size under block composition is always within a constant factor of the product of the two minimum sizes.
Both functions can be arbitrary nonconstant Boolean functions, and the inner one is applied to disjoint input blocks.
Formulas use binary AND and OR with negation, count variable occurrences, and cannot share intermediate computations.
The constant must work for every function and dimension, so dimension-dependent losses do not suffice.
The original depth conjecture and recent results for strengthened communication tasks are related but distinct statements.

definitions:
For a positive integer \(r\), a total Boolean function is a map \(h:\{0,1\}^r\to\{0,1\}\). Nonconstant means that it takes both values on its domain; it need not depend on every designated input coordinate. A De Morgan formula for \(h\) is a finite rooted tree whose internal operations are binary AND, binary OR, and unary NOT, and whose leaves are input variables or the constant bits zero and one. Its value is obtained by the usual Boolean operations from leaves to the root. It must compute \(h\) exactly on every input, with no randomness or promise on input values. There are no parity, threshold, arbitrary truth-table or unbounded-fan-in gates.

Formula size is the number of occurrences of input variables among its leaves. Positive and negated occurrences both count, and different occurrences of the same variable count separately. Constant leaves are free and can be eliminated from an optimum for a nonconstant function. NOT operations can be pushed onto variables without changing this measure. The minimum over all such formulas is \(L(h)\); it is a finite positive integer for nonconstant \(h\). No internal value can be shared between two parent operations: such reuse would produce a circuit rather than a formula.

The composed function has exactly \(mn\) designated coordinates \(x^{(j)}_i\), with \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Block coordinates are distinct and unconstrained. The same inner function \(f\) is applied to every block, and its outputs, in block order, become the inputs of \(g\). The composition symbol here means this block operation, not ordinary composition of two maps with the same domain. Both functions and their composition may be specified by arbitrary finite truth tables, and no uniformity, polynomial-time evaluability, or monotonicity is assumed.

Since both functions are nonconstant, every Boolean vector supplied to \(g\) can be realized by some collection of blocks, and the composition is nonconstant. The usual substitution bound gives \(L(g\circ f)\le L(g)L(f)\). The question is whether the ratio to that upper bound is bounded away from zero uniformly over all functions and dimensions. Equivalently, is the infimum of these positive ratios strictly positive? This infimum need not be attained. Restricting \(0<\alpha\le1\) is equivalent.

The negation says that for every positive \(\alpha\), some pair and dimensions have ratio smaller than \(\alpha\). Thus a single saving relative to exact multiplication, or even failure of one proposed constant, is insufficient to refute the claim. Allowing constant functions with the convention \(L(h)=0\) would add only trivial inequalities; their exclusion makes the ratio formulation well-defined. Minimum depth, which counts gates along a longest path, is a different measure from the number of leaves.
answer_criterion: Supply a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof or refutation of the constant-loss formula-size statement. A positive answer must establish one strictly positive factor for every permitted pair and dimensions. A negative answer must establish ratios arbitrarily close to zero, not merely a finite violation of equality or an unbounded additive saving in formula depth. Bounds for almost all functions, for special inner functions, for monotone formulas, or for a stronger communication search task do not alone prove the all-function claim. A composition inequality with a loss depending on either dimension, even polylogarithmically, is a weaker result unless upgraded to the fixed constant required here.

context_blocks.text: The book displays an absolute multiplicative constant in Conjecture 5.13. Its accompanying footnote also permits investigation of weaker losses and typical-function variants. The title and acceptance criterion identify which of those possibilities this record actually asks for.

The 1995 paper’s Open Question 4.1 asks about depth under composition and records examples with a growing additive loss in that measure. Those depth examples are not, by themselves, counterexamples to a constant-factor statement about minimum formula leaf count. The original paper and the later size formulation must be distinguished.

The 2023 paper explicitly distinguishes the original depth conjecture from the formula-size variant. Its Theorem 8.1 and Corollary 8.2 prove composition bounds involving a separate inner-function complexity measure and dimension-dependent losses. Those theorems give important restricted comparisons without supplying the universal constant asserted in this card.

The 2025 STACS result concerns strong composition of communication relations: in addition to finding a differing input bit, the answer must lie in a block where the two inner-function outputs differ. That added requirement makes a different search task. The paper explicitly says its lower bounds do not directly translate into ordinary formula-depth lower bounds, and they also do not establish the present size inequality.
